why: The supplied promotional leave-behind does not include the cited prescribing-information page as a readable source, and none of the supplied study papers establishes the exact approved-indication wording. The indication cannot be verified from the provided evidence set.

evidence_span: Both primary efficacy end points were met: after 26 weeks, baseline HbA1c (8.6%) was reduced by 1.3% with iGlarLixi and 1.1% with BIAsp 30
why: The SoliMix abstract reports the claimed treatment groups, 26-week reductions, and superiority test. The source supports the stated reductions and direction of effect; the confidence-interval convention should be checked against the paper's full results table when used externally.

evidence_span: Greater reductions in HbA1c from baseline (8.1%; 65mmol/mol) were achieved with iGlarLixi compared with iGlar and Lixi (−1.6%, −1.3%, −0.9%, respectively)
why: The cited LixiLan-O study reports reductions of 1.6% with iGlarLixi and 1.3% with insulin glargine, not a two-fold reduction. The population and Week 30 endpoint are aligned, but the promotional ratio is not supported by the reported values.
The SoliMix table reports 42.2% versus 31.8% achieving HbA1c below 7%, with an odds ratio of 1.65 and 95% CI 1.25–2.19. The claim matches the reported endpoint and study population.

evidence_span: Mean body weight decreased by 0.7 kg with iGlarLixi and increased by 0.7 kg with iGlar (1.4 kg difference, P < 0.0001).
why: The supplied LixiLan-L abstract reports a mean 0.7 kg decrease with iGlarLixi. That is not weight-neutral in the literal sense, even though it is a favorable weight change relative to insulin glargine.

The SoliMix paper reports lower incidence of ADA level-2 hypoglycemia with iGlarLixi and the promotional material's odds ratio is consistent with the reported direction and interval. The threshold and comparator match the cited claim.

evidence_span: From the LixiLan-L study, 195 patients who had been randomized to iGlarLixi were matched for age, sex, race, T2D duration, baseline body mass index, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose, insulin dose, and metformin use to 195 patients who had been randomized to a BB regimen in the Get-Goal Duo-2 trial.
why: The third panel is a post hoc propensity-score-matched comparison with a basal-bolus regimen drawn from a separate trial, not a randomized comparison against continued basal insulin. The panels show favorable weight change, but presenting all three as equivalent evidence for switching from basal insulin overstates the comparability of the underlying analyses.
